newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot power steady, Southwest higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot power steady, Southwest higher.

text.p: Spot power prices in the Northwest were largely flat, but Southwest prices were boosted by colder weather and higher natural gas prices, market sources said Tuesday.
"Our loads are up a bit, so prices are up too," said a trader at an Arizona utility.
San Diego Gas and Electric, which saw lows in its Southern California territory of 40 degrees F, was said to be offering power from gas-fired plants at $50.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
But prices in the Northwest eased slightly over the course of daily scheduling as sellers abandoned hopes for a price uptick, traders said.
"There is definitely no shortage up there," said one California utility trader.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Wednesday was quoted $17.00-18.00 per MWh, little changed from Tuesday.
Off-peak COB for Wednesday was unchanged at $9.00-10.00.
Wednesday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was quoted at $16.00-$17.00, while off-peak was at $8.00-9.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Wednesday was quoted $19.00-21.00, up from $16.50-17.50.
Off-peak PV for Wednesday was quoted $10.00-12.00 per MWh.
Wednesday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted $21.00-22.00, with off-peak at $10.00-12.00.
